question: A 72-year-old man with coronary artery disease comes to the physician because of intermittent episodes of substernal chest pain and shortness of breath. The episodes occur only when walking up stairs and resolves after resting for a few minutes. He is a delivery man and is concerned because the chest pain has impacted his ability to work. His pulse is 98/min and blood pressure is 132/77 mm Hg. Physical examination is unremarkable. An ECG shows no abnormalities. A drug that blocks which of the following receptors is most likely to prevent future episodes of chest pain from occurring?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Intermittent substernal chest pain and shortness of breath when walking up stairs" -> "Relieved by resting" -> "Likely angina pectoris" -> "Impacts ability to work" -> "Concern for coronary artery disease" -> "Episodes triggered by exertion" -> "Likely stable angina" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Delivery man with chest pain impacting work" -> "Concern for coronary artery disease" -> "Episodes triggered by exertion" -> "Likely stable angina" -> "Episodes resolve with rest" -> "Typical angina symptoms" -> "Likely due to myocardial ischemia" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Episodes of chest pain and shortness of breath when walking upstairs" -> "Relieved by rest" -> "Concern for coronary artery disease" -> "Episodes triggered by exertion" -> "Likely stable angina" -> "Episodes due to myocardial ischemia" -> 75%
enhanced_information: The patient's symptoms of intermittent substernal chest pain and shortness of breath when walking up stairs, relieved by rest, are consistent with stable angina likely due to myocardial ischemia. The most likely drug to prevent future episodes of chest pain would target Beta-1 adrenergic receptors, which are involved in regulating heart rate and contractility during exertion.
analysis: The patient's symptoms of intermittent chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion, relieved by rest, are consistent with stable angina likely due to myocardial ischemia. Beta-1 adrenergic receptors play a crucial role in regulating heart rate and contractility during exertion. Blocking these receptors can help reduce the workload on the heart and prevent future episodes of chest pain. Therefore, the most likely correct option is to target Beta-1 adrenergic receptors.
